source.condition: frozen it.skipIf(!linux), source Linux x64/arm64; this actual proof is Linux x86_64 only

command: GRIDSTATOR_TOOLCHAIN_SOURCE_KEEP=1 GRIDSTATOR_TOOLCHAIN_SOURCE_EVIDENCE=<private evidence dir> cargo +1.99.1 test --manifest-path native/Cargo.toml --locked --test worker_toolchain_source -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1
sourceState: Uncommitted shared working tree; actual immutable copied executable SHA identifies this proof, not a signed/final release.

actualProcess.nativeRolePath: private empty directory; no host act/Node/npm

sourceAssertionMap.source: Install current controller build and recognize the agent as managed
sourceAssertionMap.native: The actual host CLI is adopted by a verified InstallStore; its supervised payload reports matching embedded build ID, executable SHA-256, target, managed:true and runtime:rust.

sourceAssertionMap.source: Docker/buildx/act initially unavailable; only toolchain work is exercised
sourceAssertionMap.native: Private empty role PATH excludes host act/Node/npm. Docker is explicitly unavailable; baseline act is unavailable, tools.act is null and tools.managed is empty. No Docker workloads or services start.

sourceAssertionMap.source: toolchain act:null/node:null and a reported toolchain gap
sourceAssertionMap.native: autoUpdate:off with explicit act0.2.96 override; the actual initial behind detail says toolchain act missing →0.2.96. Native settings/toolchain views omit Node management.

sourceAssertionMap.source: Install fake act9.9.1 and observe its executable
sourceAssertionMap.native: Controller fetches actual upstream act0.2.96; an independent checksums.txt fetch agrees with the mirrored archive, the worker verifies/extracts it, persisted executable hash agrees and the installed binary executes --version.

sourceAssertionMap.source: Restart status after managed act+Node switch
sourceAssertionMap.native: Act-only changes reprobe/reconnect in the same native OS process. Same payload PID before/after; connection timestamp advances and metadata reports managed act0.2.96. No core activation is created.

sourceAssertionMap.source: Node9.9.2 path and install state node/pending/previousNode fields
sourceAssertionMap.native: The core is one verified Rust executable; its build metadata has no Node field. Current core identity remains unchanged with no pending activation/rollback during an act-only change. Stable supervisor hash matches the verified native executable after health/welcome.

sourceAssertionMap.source: Restart outside the Node-switching launcher reports a failed Node version rather than looping
sourceAssertionMap.native: A digest-correct controlled archive containing an invalid native act executable is offered through the pinned controller. Three explicit checks report target-verification errors and halt rollout without changing PID, core activation, last working act/config or restored scheduling mode. This is a synthetic negative candidate, not an upstream9.9.99 release.

sourceAssertionMap.source: After failure, managed act remains reported and there is no restarting status
sourceAssertionMap.native: Final native metadata still reports act0.2.96 managed; the actual PID is identical across all three failed checks and core activation remains unchanged.

additionalIdentityAndCoreRecoveryEvidenc.scope: Actual verified installed controller/worker role locations and automatic stable supervisor refresh after authenticated health/welcome; independent negative install-source identity and refresh tests are also recorded there.
Actual successful native core update and schema-changing crash candidate with supervisor rollback and controller DB restoration. The current tool proof does not repeat that core crash.

limits: Actual runtime target is linux/amd64. Non-host core mirror members are64-byte parser fixtures, never installed/executed.
The host core entry is the actual executable as an internal raw verified artifact, not an official packaged release archive.
The invalid9.9.99 tool archive is deliberately synthetic; outer digest is valid, inner executable target verification fails.
Three explicit failed checks establish the observed no-restart behavior; this does not claim infinite-time liveness or availability.
Node switch/path assertions are explicit plan-approved runtime/identity replacements, not unchanged v1 behavior.
No macOS act readiness, ARM Linux runtime, OS-service/reboot, signing/notarization or publication proof is implied.
